# Building B - seismic diaphragm and shear wall design basis

Design format: LRFD

## 1. Seismic basis

* **Governing Codes and Standards (`SDC-02` Rev 2 Section 1):** 2024 International Building Code (IBC) as adopted by the State of Montana (`ARM 24.301.131`), `ASCE/SEI 7-22` (*Minimum Design Loads and Associated Criteria for Buildings and Other Structures*), `ACI 318-19` (*Building Code Requirements for Structural Concrete*), `AISI S310-20` (*North American Standard for the Design of Profiled Steel Diaphragm Panels*), `AISC 360-22`, and `ASCE/SEI 37-14` for construction-stage loads. The package is prepared consistently in **Load and Resistance Factor Design (LRFD)** at strength-level seismic load ($1.0 E$, `ASCE/SEI 7-22` Section 2.3.6; `SDC-02` Section 9).
* **Risk Category and Importance Factor (`OBD-CDDC-B` Section 1.4, `SDC-02` Section 2):** Building B houses the primary data hall and, on its east side, the Lewis and Clark County consolidated 911 emergency communications dispatch floor and radio equipment room. Because the 911 tenant is an essential emergency response occupancy, Building B is assigned **Risk Category III** (`ASCE/SEI 7-22` Table 1.5-1) with a seismic importance factor of **$I_e = 1.25$** (`ASCE/SEI 7-22` Section 11.5.1, Table 1.5-2).
* **Site Class and Design Spectral Response Accelerations (`GEO-2026-071` Section 4, `SDC-02` Section 3):** Downhole shear wave velocity measurements in boring B-204 on the Building B parcel yield a time-averaged shear wave velocity in the upper 100 ft of $V_{s,100} = 905\text{ ft/s}$, classifying the site as **Site Class D** (`ASCE/SEI 7-22` Chapter 20). From the governing USGS Seismic Design Web Service output (`USGS_ASCE7-22_RiskCatIII_SiteClassD_46.6832_-111.9756.json`), the design spectral response acceleration parameters are **$S_{DS} = 0.44\text{ g}$** and **$S_{D1} = 0.24\text{ g}$** (`ASCE/SEI 7-22` Section 11.4.4). Under `ASCE/SEI 7-22` Section 11.6 (Tables 11.6-1 and 11.6-2 for Risk Category III), $S_{DS} = 0.44\text{ g}$ corresponds to SDC C while $S_{D1} = 0.24\text{ g} \ge 0.20\text{ g}$ triggers **Seismic Design Category (SDC) D**; the more severe governs (`SDC = D`).
* **Fundamental Period, Seismic Response Coefficient, and Effective Seismic Weight (`ASCE/SEI 7-22` Sections 12.7.2 & 12.8):**
  * Structural height to the roof diaphragm is $h_n = 28.0\text{ ft}$ (`A-101` Rev 3 Note 2, `PC-301` Rev 2, `DAP-2` Section 3), with a $3.0\text{ ft}$ parapet cantilevering above the deck to El. $+31.0\text{ ft}$.
  * Approximate fundamental period (`ASCE/SEI 7-22` Section 12.8.2.1, Eq. 12.8-8, Table 12.8-2 for "All other structural systems" with $C_t = 0.020, x = 0.75$):
    $$T_a = 0.020 \times (28.0)^{0.75} = 0.2434\text{ s}$$
  * Seismic response coefficient (`ASCE/SEI 7-22` Section 12.8.1.1, Eq. 12.8-2):
    $$C_s = \frac{S_{DS}}{R / I_e} = \frac{0.44}{4.0 / 1.25} = 0.1375$$
    which governs over the upper bound $S_{D1} / [T (R / I_e)] = 0.24 / (0.2434 \times 3.2) = 0.3081$ (Eq. 12.8-3) and exceeds the lower bound $0.044 S_{DS} I_e = 0.0242 \ge 0.01$ (Eq. 12.8-6).
  * Effective seismic weight $W$ (`ASCE/SEI 7-22` Section 12.7.2, `FEMA P-2192-V1` Section 7.6.1 Step 1):
    * Net roof deck area $= 240 \times 180 - 60 \times 40\text{ (RO-1)} - 80 \times 20\text{ (RO-2)} = 39,200\text{ sq ft}$ at $20\text{ psf} = 784.00\text{ kips}$.
    * Phase 1 roof-top units (`RTU-1` through `RTU-6` per `M-601` Rev 3) $= 45.00\text{ kips}$ (Phase 2 adds `RTU-7F` and `RTU-8F` at $8.0\text{ kips}$ each $= 61.00\text{ kips}$ total).
    * Precast concrete walls ($8\text{ in}$ solid normal-weight concrete at $150\text{ pcf} = 100\text{ psf}$): accounting for the lever action of the $3\text{ ft}$ parapet cantilevering above the $28\text{ ft}$ roof diaphragm (`SDC-02` Section 6, `FEMA P-2192-V1` Section 7.6.1 Step 1), the tributary wall height to the roof level is:
      $$h_{\text{trib}} = \frac{H^2}{2 h} = \frac{31.0^2}{2 \times 28.0} = \frac{961}{56} = 17.1607\text{ ft} \implies w_{\text{wall,trib}} = 100\text{ psf} \times 17.1607\text{ ft} = 1,716.07\text{ plf}$$
      This yields $411.86\text{ kips}$ each for the $240\text{ ft}$ South and North walls ($823.71\text{ kips}$ total) and $308.89\text{ kips}$ each for the $180\text{ ft}$ West and East walls ($617.79\text{ kips}$ total).
    * Total Phase 1 effective seismic weight **$W = 784.00 + 45.00 + 823.71 + 617.79 = 2,270.50\text{ kips}$** ($W_{\text{future}} = 2,286.50\text{ kips}$).
    * Design base shear (`ASCE/SEI 7-22` Eq. 12.8-1): **$V = C_s W = 0.1375 \times 2,270.50 = 312.19\text{ kips}$** ($V_{\text{future}} = 314.39\text{ kips}$).

## 2. Seismic force-resisting system

* **Selected System (`sfrs = "intermediate_precast"`):** Bearing Wall System — **Intermediate precast shear walls** (`ASCE/SEI 7-22` Table 12.2-1 / `UFC 3-301-01` Table 3-1, Line A.6; detailed per `ACI 318-19` Section 18.2.1.6 / Section 18.5 and `2024 IBC` Section 1905.3).
* **Design Coefficients (`ASCE/SEI 7-22` Table 12.2-1 / `UFC 3-301-01` Table 3-1, Line A.6):**
  * Response modification coefficient: **$R = 4.0$**
  * System overstrength factor: **$\Omega_0 = 2.5$** (tabulated), reduced by $0.5$ to **$\Omega_{0,\text{collector}} = 2.0$** for collector and drag strut design under `ASCE/SEI 7-22` Table 12.2-1 Footnote b (`UFC 3-301-01` Table 3-1 Footnote b) and `SDC-02` Section 4 because the untopped bare steel deck roof on concrete shear walls qualifies as a flexible-diaphragm structure under `ASCE/SEI 7-22` Section 12.3.1.1.
  * Deflection amplification factor: **$C_d = 4.0$**
* **Permitting Clause in SDC D at Structural Height $h_n = 28.0\text{ ft}$:** Under `ASCE/SEI 7-22` Table 12.2-1 (`UFC 3-301-01` Table 3-1, Line A.6 and Footnote i), Bearing Wall Intermediate Precast Shear Walls are permitted in **Seismic Design Category D** up to a structural height limit of **$h_n \le 40\text{ ft}$** (and $45\text{ ft}$ for single-story warehouse facilities per Footnote i). Building B has a structural height to the roof diaphragm of $h_n = 28.0\text{ ft} \le 40\text{ ft}$ (and total panel height $31.0\text{ ft} \le 40\text{ ft}$), fully satisfying the height limitation.
* **Why `intermediate_precast` is the Cost-Efficient Choice:**
  1. *Ordinary precast shear walls* (`ordinary_precast`, Line A.7, $R = 3$) are **Not Permitted (NP)** in SDC D under `ASCE/SEI 7-22` Table 12.2-1 (`UFC 3-301-01` Table 3-1 Line A.7).
  2. *Special reinforced concrete (precast) shear walls* (`special_precast`, Line A.1, $R = 5$) carry a detailing premium of $\$4,120/\text{panel}$ (`PROC-114` Rev 2) and require `ACI 318-19` Section 18.5.2 / `ACI ITG-5.2` ductile qualified joint connectors (`JC3` at $\$1,240/\text{connector}$ per `RPC-CAT-2026` Section 2). For 79 erected panels ($81$ shop-ticket panels), the SFRS premium alone is $\$325,480$ ($\$333,720$), and adding joint connectors, tie-downs, deck attachment, chords/collectors, and wall anchorage pushes the total cost over $\$490,000$, violating the hard $\$395,000$ capital cap in `PROC-114` and `OBD-CDDC-B` Section 5.6.
  3. *Intermediate precast shear walls* (`intermediate_precast`, Line A.6, $R = 4$) carry a detailing premium of $\$1,850/\text{panel}$ ($\$146,150$ for 79 panels, saving $\$179,330$ on SFRS detailing alone) and allow `JC1` (`RPC-24` at $\$385/\text{connector}$), achieving full code compliance at an installed cost of **$\$353,628.00$** ($\$41,372$ below the $\$395,000$ budget cap).

## 3. As-built geometry

Every discrepancy across the project documents was cross-checked and resolved using the governing hierarchy established in `T-2026-118`, `SDC-02` Rev 2, `RFI-041`, `CDDC-SV-2026-041`, and `ERL-2026-08`:

1. **South Wall Dock Openings D-3 & D-4 and Pier S5 (`RFI-041`, `ERL-2026-08`, `ScanB_2026-08-07_interior.ply` vs. `PC-101` Rev 2, `PC-301` Rev 2, `A-101` Rev 3, `S-201` Rev 2):**
   * *Conflict:* Record drawings detail five $14.0\text{ ft}$ dock doors `D-1` to `D-5` with $16.0\text{ ft}$ piers between them (`D-3` at $X = 78.0..92.0\text{ ft}$, `D-4` at $X = 108.0..122.0\text{ ft}$, and Pier `S5` at $X = 122.0..138.0\text{ ft}$, length $16.0\text{ ft}$).
   * *Resolution:* Per `RFI-041`, `ERL-2026-08`, and registration of the interior laser scan `ScanB_2026-08-07_interior.ply` to the building grid via control targets `CP-1` to `CP-4` (`CDDC-SV-2026-041`), `D-3` was erected $15.5\text{ ft}$ wide ($X = 78.0..93.5\text{ ft}$), shifting `S4` to $X = 93.5..109.5\text{ ft}$ ($16.0\text{ ft}$) and `D-4` to $X = 109.5..123.5\text{ ft}$ ($14.0\text{ ft}$), which closes full-height Pier `S5` (between `D-4` and `D-5`) to **$14.5\text{ ft}$** ($X = 123.5..138.0\text{ ft}$). The seven as-built piers on Wall S have lengths **$18.0, 16.0, 16.0, 16.0, 14.5, 44.0, 40.0\text{ ft}$**.
2. **North Wall Louver Opening L-2 (`RFI-041`, `PCS-014` Rev B, `ERL-2026-08`, `ScanB_2026-08-07_interior.ply` vs. `PC-101` Rev 2, `PC-301` Rev 2, `A-101` Rev 3, `S-201` Rev 2):**
   * *Conflict:* Record drawings show louver `L-2` as $12.0\text{ ft} \times 10.0\text{ ft}$ at $X = 156.0..168.0\text{ ft}$.
   * *Resolution:* Per `PCS-014` (Ticket Rev B), `ERL-2026-08`, `RFI-041`, and the 3D scan, `L-2` was recast to **$16.0\text{ ft} \times 10.0\text{ ft}$** ($Z = 14.0..24.0\text{ ft}$) at **$X = 154.0..170.0\text{ ft}$**. Because `L-1` ($X = 60.0..72.0\text{ ft}$) and `L-2` ($X = 154.0..170.0\text{ ft}$) do not reach the foundation ($Z = 14..24\text{ ft}$), they act as spandrel segments (`N3` = $12.0\text{ ft}$, `N5` = $16.0\text{ ft}$) with flexural and shear rigidities factored by the solid height fraction $(28 - 10)/28 = 18/28$ per `DAP-2` Section 3, while full-height piers are `N1` ($24.0\text{ ft}$), `N2` ($32.0\text{ ft}$), `N4` ($82.0\text{ ft}$), and `N6` ($70.0\text{ ft}$).
3. **West Wall Electrical Yard Opening EY-1 (`RFI-041`, `ERL-2026-08` FC-018, `ScanB_2026-08-07_interior.ply` vs. `PC-101` Rev 2, `PC-301` Rev 2, `A-101` Rev 3, `S-201` Rev 2):**
   * *Conflict:* Record drawings show `EY-1` as $40.0\text{ ft} \times 20.0\text{ ft}$ at $Y = 66.0..106.0\text{ ft}$ (giving north pier `W3` = $74.0\text{ ft}$).
   * *Resolution:* Per Field Change FC-018 in `ERL-2026-08`, `RFI-041`, and the 3D scan, `EY-1` was widened on site to **$44.0\text{ ft}$** ($Y = 66.0..110.0\text{ ft}$), reducing full-height Pier `W3` to **$70.0\text{ ft}$** ($Y = 110.0..180.0\text{ ft}$), alongside `W1` ($12.0\text{ ft}$, $Y = 0.0..12.0\text{ ft}$) and `W2` ($50.0\text{ ft}$, $Y = 16.0..66.0\text{ ft}$).
4. **Risk Category & Ground Motion Basis (`SDC-02` Rev 2, `OBD-CDDC-B`, `GEO-2026-071`, `USGS_ASCE7-22_RiskCatIII_SiteClassD...json` vs. `A-101` cover block, `GEO-2019-118`, `SM-2019-04`, `USGS_ASCE7-16...json`, `USGS_ASCE7-22_RiskCatII...json`):**
   * *Resolution:* Risk Category III ($I_e = 1.25$), Site Class D ($V_{s,100} = 905\text{ ft/s}$), `ASCE/SEI 7-22`, $S_{DS} = 0.44\text{ g}$, $S_{D1} = 0.24\text{ g}$, and SDC D govern. Parcel 4B report `GEO-2019-118`, Building A summary `SM-2019-04`, and Risk Category II / `ASCE 7-16` files are superseded/inapplicable.
5. **Roof Mechanical Equipment (`A-101` Rev 3, `M-601` Rev 3, `OBD-CDDC-B` Section 2.2 vs. `A-101` Rev 1 in `90_archive`):**
   * *Resolution:* `A-101` Rev 1 (`90_archive`) is superseded (missed `RTU-5` and `RTU-6`). `M-601` Rev 3 governs with 6 Phase 1 units ($45.0\text{ kips}$) for `base` and `erection` cases and 2 additional reserved Phase 2 units (`RTU-7F`, `RTU-8F`, $+16.0\text{ kips} = 61.0\text{ kips}$ total) for `future` cases.
6. **Diaphragm Idealisation and Design Method (`PR-07`, `SDC-02` Sections 5 & 10, `DAP-2` vs. standalone flexible idealisation or `ASCE 7-22` Sections 12.10.3 / 12.10.4):**
   * *Resolution:* Per Peer Review Comment `PR-07` and `SDC-02` Section 10, design forces are taken from the **envelope** of flexible, rigid, and semi-rigid idealisations (`DAP-2` Section 6.3), while deflections are reported from the semi-rigid model (`DAP-2` Section 6.2). Traditional diaphragm provisions (`ASCE/SEI 7-22` Sections 12.10.1 and 12.10.2) govern per `SDC-02` Section 5.

## 4. Analysis

The lateral analysis strictly implements the two-stage protocol of **`DAP-2` Rev 1**:
* **Stage A — Jointed Precast Wall Segments (`DAP-2` Section 3):** Each continuous wall segment of length $L$ is subdivided into panels up to $10.0\text{ ft}$ wide ($t = 8\text{ in}$, $h = 28.0\text{ ft} = 336\text{ in}$, $f'_c = 6,000\text{ psi}$, $E_c = 57,000\sqrt{f'_c} = 4,415.2\text{ ksi}$, $G_c = E_c / 2.4 = 1,839.7\text{ ksi}$, $I = 0.50 I_g$ per `ACI 318-19` Table 6.6.3.1.1(a), $A_v = \frac{5}{6} A_g$, axial stiffness $k_{vv} = E_c A_g / h$). Spandrel segments (`N3` at `L-1`, `N5` at `L-2`, `E3` at `L-3`, where $10\text{ ft}$ high louvers do not reach the foundation) retain their length with $EI$ and $GA_v$ factored by the solid height fraction $(28 - 10)/28 = 18/28$. Vertical joints have spring stiffness $k_{\text{joint}} = n_{\text{conn}} k_{\text{conn}} = 1 \times 210 = 210\text{ kip/in}$ (`JC1`). Our Stage A implementation reproduces Verification Example `VP-1` (`DAP-2` Appendix A) to all published digits ($k_{\text{seg}} = 1,279.4\text{ kip/in}$, end joint shear $= 0.2630\text{ kip/kip}$, middle joint shear $= 0.2527\text{ kip/kip}$, Panel 1 base moment $= 88.91\text{ kip-in/kip}$, Panel 1 axial force $= 0.2630\text{ kip/kip}$, isolated pier $k_{\text{seg}} = 769.2\text{ kip/in}$).
* **Stage B — Roof Diaphragm (`DAP-2` Sections 4–6):** The $240\text{ ft} \times 180\text{ ft}$ roof is meshed with $10\text{ ft} \times 10\text{ ft}$ 4-node plane-stress membrane elements ($24 \times 18 = 432$ grid cells; 40 elements inside `RO-1` $[96..156]\times[108..148]$ and `RO-2` $[36..116]\times[36..56]$ removed, leaving 392 active elements $= 39,200\text{ sq ft}$). Each element has $D = \text{diag}(A', A', G')$ with $A' = 1,740\text{ kip/in}$, $\nu = 0$, and $G'$ from `BDS-2026` Table 4 for its zone `Z1..Z12`. Chords, collectors, and opening framing (`CH-*`, `DR-*`, `OP-*`) are 2-node bar elements with $E = 29,000\text{ ksi}$. Wall segment springs $k_{\text{seg}}$ act along their respective boundary nodes.
* **Accidental Torsion and Envelope (`DAP-2` Sections 5 & 6):** A $5\%$ accidental eccentricity ($\pm 9.0\text{ ft}$ in Y for X-loading; $\pm 12.0\text{ ft}$ in X for Y-loading, or $\pm 9.0\text{ ft}$ in erection case `S12`) is applied as a mass-proportional rotational force field about the center of mass. In all cases, $\delta_{\max} / \delta_{\text{avg}} \le 1.20$ in the rigid model, so $A_x = 1.0$. Every design force is taken from the **envelope** of the `flexible`, `rigid` ($10^7$ membrane stiffness), and `semi-rigid` models (`DAP-2` Section 6.3), with 100%/30% orthogonal combinations applied to `S05`, `S06`, `S09`, and `S10` (`DAP-2` Section 6.4).

## 5. Diaphragm and wall forces

* **Diaphragm Design Forces (`ASCE/SEI 7-22` Section 12.10.1.1):**
  * Since $C_s = 0.1375$ lies between $0.2 S_{DS} I_e = 0.1100$ (Eq. 12.10-2) and $0.4 S_{DS} I_e = 0.2200$ (Eq. 12.10-3), $F_{px} / w_{px} = 0.1375$ governs:
    * **X (E-W, base):** $w_{px,X} = 1,446.79\text{ kips}$, $F_{px,X} = 198.93\text{ kips}$, distributed over the $180\text{ ft}$ N-S span as **$w_{px,X} = 1,105.18\text{ plf}$** (future: $w_{px,X} = 1,462.79\text{ kips}$, $F_{px,X} = 201.13\text{ kips}$, $1,117.41\text{ plf}$).
    * **Y (N-S, base):** $w_{px,Y} = 1,652.71\text{ kips}$, $F_{px,Y} = 227.25\text{ kips}$, distributed over the $240\text{ ft}$ E-W span as **$w_{px,Y} = 946.87\text{ plf}$** (future: $w_{px,Y} = 1,668.71\text{ kips}$, $F_{px,Y} = 229.45\text{ kips}$, $956.03\text{ plf}$).
* **Envelope Wall Line Forces (`S01`–`S12`):**
  * **South Wall (`S`):** Max envelope shear $= 104.48\text{ kips}$ (`S09`), $104.47\text{ kips}$ (`S02` $101.36\text{ kips}$ + $0.3 \times$ `S04`).
  * **North Wall (`N`):** Max envelope shear $= 122.91\text{ kips}$ (`S09`), $119.03\text{ kips}$ (`S07`).
  * **West Wall (`W`):** Max envelope shear $= 147.82\text{ kips}$ (`S10`), $147.61\text{ kips}$ (`S06`); in erection case `S12` (deck east of $X = 180\text{ ft}$ unfastened), Wall W resists $100\%$ of the fastened diaphragm N-S shear ($84.20\text{ kips}$).
  * **East Wall (`E`):** Max envelope shear $= 155.77\text{ kips}$ (`S10`), $125.24\text{ kips}$ (`S08`).
* **Deck Attachment Zones (`BDS-2026` Table 4, $\phi = 0.60$ LRFD):**
  * `P5` ($\phi S_n = 1,101\text{ plf}$, $G' = 61.0\text{ kip/in}$) in west-end zones `Z1`, `Z5`, `Z9` (max demand $982.0\text{ plf}$ in `Z1`, utilization $0.892$, and provides high shear rigidity at the root of the erection-stage cantilever in `S12`).
  * `P4` ($\phi S_n = 852\text{ plf}$, $G' = 49.0\text{ kip/in}$) in `Z2`, `Z4`, `Z8`, `Z10`, `Z12` (max demand $767.7\text{ plf}$ in `S01..S12` and $821.7\text{ plf}$ across all 24 orthogonal combinations, utilization $0.901$ / $0.964$).
  * `P3` ($\phi S_n = 663\text{ plf}$, $G' = 38.0\text{ kip/in}$) in interior zones `Z3`, `Z6`, `Z7`, `Z11` (max demand $602.2\text{ plf}$ in `Z11`, utilization $0.908$).
  * Maximum semi-rigid amplified deflection at the top of the panel is **$C_d \delta / I_e = 3.45\text{ in} \le 4.00\text{ in}$** across `S01`–`S12` (and $3.96\text{ in} \le 4.00\text{ in}$ across all 24 possible combinations), satisfying `SDC-02` Section 7.
* **Chords, Collectors, and Drag Struts (`S-201` Rev 2, `SDC-02` Section 5):** Continuous `C1` (`L4x4x3/8`, $A = 2.86\text{ in}^2$, $\phi_t P_n = 92.66\text{ kips}$ LRFD) is provided on all 20 lines (`CH-S/N/W/E`, `DR-S1/S2/N1/N2/W1/W2/E1/E2`, `OP-1S/N/W/E`, `OP-2S/N/W/E`). Maximum chord demand is $56.75\text{ kips} \le 92.66\text{ kips}$ (`CH-S`), and maximum amplified collector/drag strut demand ($\Omega_0 = 2.0$) is $48.70\text{ kips} \le 92.66\text{ kips}$ (`DR-W2`).

## 6. Wall anchorage and the parapet cantilever

* **Lever Action of the Parapet Cantilever (`SDC-02` Section 6, `FEMA P-2192-V1` Section 7.6.1 Step 1):** Each $8\text{ in}$ precast panel ($100\text{ psf}$) spans $h = 28.0\text{ ft}$ from the foundation to the roof deck and cantilevers $p = 3.0\text{ ft}$ above the deck ($H = 31.0\text{ ft}$). Taking moments about the base support ($z = 0$):
  * Total wall weight tributary to the roof diaphragm per foot of wall:
    $$W_p = 100\text{ psf} \times \frac{31.0^2}{2 \times 28.0}\text{ ft} = 1,716.07\text{ plf}$$
  * Portion from the wall below the roof deck ($z \in [0, 28\text{ ft}]$): $100 \times (28.0 / 2) = 1,400.00\text{ plf}$.
  * Portion delivered to the roof by the wall above the top of deck (parapet weight plus cantilever lever action about the base):
    $$w_{\text{parapet,transfer}} = 100\text{ psf} \times \frac{31.0^2 - 28.0^2}{2 \times 28.0}\text{ ft} = 300\text{ plf} \times \frac{29.5\text{ ft}}{28.0\text{ ft}} = 316.07\text{ plf}$$
* **Out-of-Plane Wall Anchorage Force (`ASCE/SEI 7-22` Section 12.11.2.1, `UFC 3-301-01` Figure 3-1):**
  * Because the flexible diaphragm span exceeds $100\text{ ft}$ in both directions ($L_{f,X} = 180\text{ ft}$, $L_{f,Y} = 240\text{ ft}$), $k_a = \min(1.0 + L_f / 100, 2.0) = 2.0$ in both directions.
  * Under `ASCE/SEI 7-22` Section 12.11.2.1:
    $$F_p = \max\left(0.4 S_{DS} k_a I_e W_p,\; 0.2 k_a I_e W_p\right) = \max(0.44,\; 0.50) \times 1,716.07\text{ plf} = 0.50 \times 1,716.07 = 858.04\text{ plf}$$
    (Since $S_{DS} = 0.44 < 0.50$, the minimum $0.2 k_a I_e W_p = 0.50 W_p$ governs over $0.4 S_{DS} k_a I_e W_p = 0.44 W_p$.)
* **Wall Anchor Selection and Subdiaphragms (`RPC-CAT-2026` Section 7, `S-201` Notes 1 & 4, `ASCE/SEI 7-22` Section 12.11.2.2.1):**
  * Using `WA1` ($3/4\text{ in}$ joist seat anchor, $T_n = 9.4\text{ kips}$, $\phi T_n = 0.75 \times 9.4 = 7.05\text{ kips}$ LRFD) at the joist seat spacing of **$6.0\text{ ft}$ o.c.**, the demand per anchor is $858.04\text{ plf} \times 6.0\text{ ft} = 5.15\text{ kips} \le 7.05\text{ kips}$ ($D/C = 0.730$).
  * Subdiaphragms are $60.0\text{ ft}$ span by $30.0\text{ ft}$ depth ($L_s / d_s = 60 / 30 = 2.0 \le 2.5$ maximum per `ASCE/SEI 7-22` Section 12.11.2.2.1) with continuous ties across the diaphragm at every column/su

steps.message:
The delegated lateral design and seismic analysis package for **Building B** at the Continental Divide Data Center has been completed and packaged in `/filesystem/final_batch4__structural_task6_seismic_diaphragm_shear__blind/output/submission.zip` (containing `design_record.json`, `diaphragm_plan.dxf`, `seismic_calculations.xlsx`, `constraint_register.xlsx`, and `design_basis.md`).

### 1. Deliverables Produced

* `/filesystem/final_batch4__structural_task6_seismic_diaphragm_shear__blind/output/submission.zip`: Archive containing the five deliverable files at the root level:
  * `design_record.json`: Machine-readable design selections, resolved document conflicts, as-built pier schedules, seismic basis parameters, and reported envelope forces, shears, anchor demands, and installed cost.
  * `diaphragm_plan.dxf`: Two roof diaphragm plan views (E-W loading and N-S loading, in feet) on layers `DIAPHRAGM_SHEAR`, `WALL_FORCE`, `CHORD`, `COLLECTOR`, `DECK_ZONE`, `GRID`, and `TITLE`, showing distributed diaphragm loads $w_{px}$, zoned attachment patterns and unit shears, applied shear wall loads $F_x$, chord/collector/drag strut runs with axial demands, and the LRFD title/revision block.
  * `seismic_calculations.xlsx`: Calculation workbook with sheets `WEIGHTS`, `BASE_SHEAR`, `DIAPHRAGM_FORCES`, `WALL_FORCES`, `PARAPET_ANCHORAGE`, and `CHORD_FORCES`.
  * `constraint_register.xlsx`: Register of 62 governing requirements with document numbers, clauses/tables/sections, values, bound items, and hard/soft classifications (excluding superseded/archive documents).
  * `design_basis.md`: Narrative documenting the seismic basis, SFRS selection, as-built conflict resolutions, `DAP-2` two-stage analysis verification, diaphragm and wall demands, parapet cantilever anchorage, governing checks per wall line, installed cost breakdown, and rejected alternatives.

---

### 2. Governing Documents & Conflict Resolutions

* **Risk Category & Importance Factor (`OBD-CDDC-B` Section 1.4, `SDC-02` Rev 2 Section 2):** Risk Category **III** ($I_e = 1.25$, `ASCE/SEI 7-22` Table 1.5-2) governs due to the county 911 emergency communications tenant, superseding the schematic Risk Category II block on `A-101` and `USGS_ASCE7-22_RiskCatII_SiteClassD_46.6832_-111.9756.json`.
* **Site Class & Ground Motion (`GEO-2026-071` Section 4, `SDC-02` Section 3, `USGS_ASCE7-22_RiskCatIII_SiteClassD_46.6832_-111.9756.json`):** Site Class **D** ($V_{s,100} = 905\text{ ft/s}$), $S_{DS} = 0.44\text{ g}$, $S_{D1} = 0.24\text{ g}$, and **SDC D** (`ASCE/SEI 7-22` Section 11.6) govern for Building B, superseding the 2019 Parcel 4B report `GEO-2019-118` and Building A summary `SM-2019-04`.
* **As-Built Erected Geometry (`RFI-041`, `ERL-2026-08`, `CDDC-SV-2026-041`, `PCS-014` Rev B, `ScanB_2026-08-07_interior.ply`):**
  * **South Wall (`S`):** Dock door `D-3` was erected at $15.5\text{ ft}$ wide ($X = 78.0..93.5\text{ ft}$) and `D-4` at $X = 109.5..123.5\text{ ft}$ ($14.0\text{ ft}$), closing Pier `S5` between `D-4` and `D-5` to **$14.5\text{ ft}$** ($X = 123.5..138.0\text{ ft}$). As-built pier lengths: $18.0, 16.0, 16.0, 16.0, 14.5, 44.0, 40.0\text{ ft}$.
  * **North Wall (`N`):** Panel `N-12` was recast to shop ticket Rev B with louver `L-2` widened to **$16.0\text{ ft} \times 10.0\text{ ft}$** at $X = 154.0..170.0\text{ ft}$ ($Z = 14..24\text{ ft}$). As-built segments: `N1` ($24.0\text{ ft}$ pier), `N2` ($32.0\text{ ft}$ pier), `N3` ($12.0\text{ ft}$ spandrel at `L-1`), `N4` ($82.0\text{ ft}$ pier), `N5` ($16.0\text{ ft}$ spandrel at `L-2`), and `N6` ($70.0\text{ ft}$ pier).
  * **West Wall (`W`):** Opening `EY-1` was widened on site (FC-018) from $40.0\text{ ft}$ to **$44.0\text{ ft}$** ($Y = 66.0..110.0\text{ ft}$), reducing north pier `W3` from $74.0\text{ ft}$ to **$70.0\text{ ft}$** (with `W1` = $12.0\text{ ft}$ and `W2` = $50.0\text{ ft}$).
  * **East Wall (`E`):** As detailed (`E1` = $72.0\text{ ft}$ pier, `E2` = $22.0\text{ ft}$ pier, `E3` = $12.0\text{ ft}$ spandrel at `L-3`, `E4` = $30.0\text{ ft}$ pier, `E5` = $26.0\text{ ft}$ pier).

---

### 3. Key Engineering & Cost Results (LRFD)

* **SFRS Selection:** **Intermediate precast concrete shear walls** (`intermediate_precast`, Bearing Wall System, `ASCE/SEI 7-22` Table 12.2-1 / `UFC 3-301-01` Table 3-1 Line A.6: $R = 4.0$, $\Omega_0 = 2.5$ reduced by $0.5$ to $\Omega_{0,\text{collector}} = 2.0$ per Footnote b, $C_d = 4.0$), permitted in SDC D up to $h_n \le 40\text{ ft}$ (Building B $h_n = 28.0\text{ ft}$).
* **Seismic Weight, Base Shear & Diaphragm Loads:**
  * Tributary wall height including $3.0\text{ ft}$ parapet cantilever lever action (`FEMA P-2192-V1` Section 7.6.1 Step 1): $h_{\text{trib}} = 31.0^2 / (2 \times 28.0) = 17.1607\text{ ft}$ ($w_{\text{wall,trib}} = 1,716.07\text{ plf}$, of which **$316.07\text{ plf}$** is delivered by the parapet above the deck).
  * Fundamental period $T_a = 0.020 (28.0)^{0.75} = 0.2434\text{ s}$; seismic response coefficient $C_s = 0.44 / (4.0 / 1.25) = 0.1375$.
  * Phase 1 effective seismic weight $W = 2,270.50\text{ kips}$ ($V = 312.19\text{ kips}$); Phase 2 future weight $W_{\text{future}} = 2,286.50\text{ kips}$ ($V_{\text{future}} = 314.39\text{ kips}$).
  * Diaphragm design forces (`ASCE/SEI 7-22` Section 12.10.1.1, $F_{px}/w_{px} = 0.1375$):
    * **E-W (`X`, base):** $w_{px,X} = 1,446.79\text{ kips}$, $F_{px,X} = 198.93\text{ kips}$, **$w_{px,X} = 1,105.18\text{ plf}$** over the $180\text{ ft}$ N-S span.
    * **N-S (`Y`, base):** $w_{px,Y} = 1,652.71\text{ kips}$, $F_{px,Y} = 227.25\text{ kips}$, **$w_{px,Y} = 946.87\text{ plf}$** over the $240\text{ ft}$ E-W span.
* **Deck Attachment, Chords/Collectors, Connections & Anchorage:**
  * **Deck Zones (`BDS-2026` Table 4, $\phi = 0.60$):** `P5` ($\phi S_n = 1,101\text{ plf}$, $G' = 61.0\text{ kip/in}$) in `Z1, Z5, Z9`; `P4` ($\phi S_n = 852\text{ plf}$, $G' = 49.0\text{ kip/in}$) in `Z2, Z4, Z8, Z10, Z12`; `P3` ($\phi S_n = 663\text{ plf}$, $G' = 38.0\text{ kip/in}$) in `Z3, Z6, Z7, Z11`. Max zone shear is $982.0\text{ plf} \le 1,101.0\text{ plf}$ (`Z1`), and max amplified semi-rigid deflection is $C_d \delta / I_e = 3.45\text{ in} \le 4.00\text{ in}$ (`S12`).
  * **Chords, Collectors & Drag Struts:** Continuous `C1` (`L4x4x3/8`, $\phi P_n = 92.66\text{ kips}$) on all 20 scheduled lines (`CH-*`, `DR-*`, `OP-*`); max chord demand $= 56.75\text{ kips}$, max amplified collector demand ($\Omega_0 = 2.0$) $= 48.70\text{ kips}$.
  * **Wall Panel Connections & Anchorage (`RPC-CAT-2026`):** `JC1` (`RPC-24`, $\phi V_n = 18.0\text{ kips}$, $k = 210\text{ kip/in}$) at $1\text{ connector/joint}$; `BA2` (`4-#8 dowel + grouted sleeve`, $\phi T_n = 66.0\text{ kips}$) at $1\text{ per panel}$; out-of-plane wall anchors `WA1` ($\phi T_n = 7.05\text{ kips}$) at $6.0\text{ ft}$ o.c. ($k_a = 2.0$, $F_p = 858.04\text{ plf}$, demand $= 5.15\text{ kips/anchor}$) with $60\text{ ft} \times 30\text{ ft}$ subdiaphragms ($2.0:1 \le 2.5:1$).
  * **Installed Cost (`PROC-114` Rev 2):** **$\$353,628.00\text{ USD}$** ($\$41,372.00$ below the $\$395,000.00$ capital cap).
